content:
pagerduty-bot: [PAGER] incident INC-2026-0415: high packet loss / BGP flaps observed affecting us-west-2 -> transit provider (TransitCo). Severity: high. Affected: customer traffic to region us-west-2 (APIs + web). Paging netops-oncall and infra-sre. Details: sudden upstream route withdrawals, elevated retransmits.

max: Ack'd. I'm oncall. Starting a quick triage. Where are we seeing loss?

alex: Cloud metrics show spike in TCP retransmits from our egress clusters in us-west-2 at 09:12 UTC. BGP table shows a flurry of withdraws for TransitCo prefixes.

marta: Confirming customers reporting increased 5xxs and higher tail latencies in us-west-2. CS ticket #7892 opened. @dave-cs can you summarize impacted customers?

dave-cs: Two mid-market customers reported degraded API responses; one high-traffic SaaS customer seeing errors for writes to objects. Providing logs to eng.

samir: I'm pulling bgp state from our edge routers. Output snippet:```bash
# show ip bgp neighbors 203.0.113.5 advertised-routes
Neighbor 203.0.113.5: est. 00:42:12
  Received 24 routes, 7 withdrawn in last 5m
  Flap counter: 12
```

max: Looks like the flap is upstream (TransitCo). Can we try short mitigation: shift egress for critical prefixes to backup provider (PeerB) and announce more-specifics to steer?

alex: Preparing announcement plan. Two options: 1) prep traffic steering via route-map + MED to prefer PeerB, 2) more specific /24 announces for critical customer prefixes (risk: attracts full traffic). What's tolerance?

marta: We should avoid more specifics unless necessary. Start with MED + local-preference to PeerB for affected customer prefixes. Also increase retransmit timeouts in our retry policy temporarily?

max: Agreed. I'll coordinate with netops to patch route maps. Oncall-roster: @samir you're primary for the netops change, @alex you handle canary validation and metrics.

samir: Applying change now. Pushing route-map to edge-01 and edge-02. Commands:```bash
set policy route-map STEER-TO-PEERB permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list AFFECTED_CUSTOMERS
 set local-preference 200
```

samir: Pushed to edge-01, propagating. edge-02 next.

alex: Watching metrics: retransmits trending down on edge-01 within 45s. HTTP 5xx rate dropping from 12% -> 6% for canary subset.

katie: I'm spinning up temporary extra capacity in us-west-2 to absorb retries and reduce queueing. Autoscale look fine but adding a buffer.

dave-cs: Customer A reports improvement on their end. Thanks team.

max: Good. We should open a support case with TransitCo. Samir, can you gather the bgp timestamps and syslog extracts?

samir: Collecting:```text
09:11:58 withdraw prefix 198.51.100.0/22 from 203.0.113.5
09:12:03 withdraw prefix 198.51.101.0/24 from 203.0.113.5
09:12:15 update flap detected with holdtime expired
```

max: Filing ticket with TransitCo now. Include pcap? We have sample tcpdump from egress-01 capturing retransmits and BGP TCP resets. Uploading to case.

alex: Note: we saw a small DNS skew for internal service discovery in us-west-2 during the flap — internal DNS queries to edge service returned stale EC2 egress IP for ~18s due to cache timing. Probably contributed to retries. DNS team FYI.

marta: Customer impact severity: degraded API responses for ~10-15 minutes for affected traffic, partial recovery after steering. Will draft incident summary for postmortem.

dave-cs: Flagging one enterprise customer requires a formal incident notification. I'll prepare a customer-facing timeline.

samir: edge-02 changes applied. Route stability holding at ~09:18 UTC. BGP flap counter stable.

max: Can we verify cross-region failover behavior? Any traffic that should have automatically used another region?
alex: Our routing policy allows cross-region fallback but only for specific services (replication, not reads). So some traffic stayed local and hit the flap. We should consider temporary global failover for critical APIs if provider instability continues.

katie: I'll keep extra capacity online and increase health-check frequency so we can detect early regressions.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-0415 status update: mitigation in progress, traffic steering to PeerB applied, customer impacts reduced. Next update in 10m or on resolution.

max: Good progress. Let's hold for 30m after stability to consider resolved. Samir, post the support case number when TransitCo responds. Alex — collect metrics for postmortem (packet loss, BGP withdraws, HTTP 5xx timeline). Marta/Dave — coordinate customer comms.

samir: TransitCo case created: TCK-56981. They acknowledge degraded transit in their west backbone and are performing root cause analysis. Will update within 60m.

alex: Captured needed traces and uploaded to S3 path s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-0415/ (pcap + bgp-logs + metrics). Setting retention 30d for incident team.

marta: Drafting initial post-incident Slack summary and will schedule a blameless postmortem. Initial RCA points: upstream transit instability + transient DNS cache skew + partial routing policy coverage for cross-region fallback.

dave-cs: Sent customer notification to affected tenant contacts with ETA for RFO.

max: Marking this thread as mitigation-in-progress. Keep updates here. If flaps return or TransitCo response unacceptable, we'll escalate to execs and consider temporary full failover to PeerB. Thanks all. :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: [PAGER RESOLVED] INC-2026-0415 marked mitigated at 09:31 UTC. Root cause investigation in progress.
